minutes.headline: Commission continued three hearings and set a May 7 continuance for 67 Island Road after members signaled the patio, wall and stairs can't be grandfathered.
minutes.summary: The Conservation Commission heard the Table Rock trailhead parking NOI (994 Northfield Road), approved the 780 Northfield Road culvert and wetland replication NOI with DEP conditions, and continued the 67 Island Road RDA and 213 Electric Ave NOI. Most discussion was the 67 Island Road deck, wall, patio and stairs, where members agreed the work is not grandfathered and floated revegetation as a compromise. New business covered a DEP training on April 30 and the end of fully remote meetings in April.

attendees.role: member (newly appointed; not voting on continued hearings)

public_comment.stated_role: property owner, Settlers Crossing Golf Course
public_comment.topic: Concerns about the trailhead parking's drainage impact on golf holes, golfers or trail users straying onto the course, and golf balls.
Worried about monitoring of an out-of-sight parking area, loitering, police calls, and trespass onto the second tee.
Asked how skunk cabbage was recorded on the December wetland delineation at the Table Rock site.
Letter from John Fortune (50 Hemlock) read by the chair, citing GIS and aerial photos showing 67 Island Road structures closer to the lake and asking about runoff and the high water mark distance.

decisions.decision: The 32 Hemlock Drive and 390 Howard Street items and the 7 PM appointment are carried to March 19; the 215 Sunset Drive hearing was delayed because abutter notices did not go out in time.
The Table Rock applicant will enlarge the wetland replication area and add a dense understory planting buffer toward the golf course.
The commission leans toward finding the 67 Island Road work not grandfathered and invites the applicants to return with a counter-proposal; the hearing is continued to May 7.
The 213 Electric Ave applicant is to add a planting schedule and a limit-of-work callout to the plan.
A DEP training for the commission is tentatively set for April 30 at 7 PM in place of a meeting; a poll via Outlook will choose topics.
Meetings return to in-person with hybrid in April; the commission discussed the quorum rule that remote members do not count.

what_happened.line: The Conservation Commission approved the 780 Northfield Road culvert replacement and wetland replication with DEP's special conditions of two-year monitoring and 75% survival.
The 67 Island Road hearing was continued to May 7 after members leaned toward finding the patio, wall and stairs not grandfathered and invited a counter-proposal.
The Table Rock trailhead parking hearing at 994 Northfield Road was continued to March 19; the applicant will enlarge the replication area and add a planted buffer.
The 213 Electric Ave hearing was continued to March 19, with the applicant to add a planting schedule and a limit-of-work callout to the plan.
Meetings return to in-person with hybrid in April, and a DEP training is tentatively set for April 30 at 7 PM.

why_it_matters: Work near wetlands and Lunenburg's lakes needs commission approval, and the 67 Island Road discussion shows that older structures in the buffer may not be treated as grandfathered, which bears on any lakefront owner with similar work.
The Table Rock trailhead parking proposal is still open, so abutters and golfers raising drainage, trespass and monitoring concerns have another hearing at which to comment.
watch_next: March 19: continued hearings for 994 Northfield Road (Table Rock) and 213 Electric Ave, plus the items carried over from this meeting.
May 7: continued 67 Island Road hearing, where the applicants may bring a counter-proposal such as revegetation.
